name: Ubykh
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 4 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Vogt, Hans. 1963. Dictionnaire de la langue oubykh, avec introduction phonologique, index français-oubykh, textes oubykhs. (Instituttet for sammenlignende kulturforskning, Serie B: Skrifter LII.) Oslo: Universitetsforlaget.
catalog_locator: Introduction phonologique, section 'L'accent', pp. 31-33; deciding statement p. 32, continuation and fixed/mobile accent classes p. 33
catalog_quote: Les conclusions auxquelles nous sommes arrivé, sont les suivantes: Dans un mot polysyllabique prononcé isolément, il y a toujours une syllabe qui est mise en valeur par un accent expiratoire, relativement faible et souvent difficile à saisir. Les informateurs eux-mêmes n'en semblent pas conscients, et y paient en tout cas peu d'attention ... Les cas où un informateur averti comme Tevfik Esenç de lui-même signale une différenciation par l'accent sont exceptionnels; l'on constate, en effet, que le cas se présente rarement. ... L'accent a en tout cas un rendement fonctionnel très modeste. ... Rien ne laisse prédire la place de l'accent dans un mot donné, toutes les syllabes peuvent porter l'accent. La situation se complique du fait que dans le procès morphologique l'accent d'une forme peut se déplacer. Certains monosyllabes gardent ainsi un accent fixe sur la syllabe radicale dans la forme définie, d'autres le reportent sur l'article (ou sur les préfixes possessifs ou démonstratifs). [p. 33] Les monosyllabes à accent fixe semblent être à peu près deux fois plus nombreux que ceux à accent mobile. Les monosyllabes à consonne finale sont en général à accent fixe.
world_status: statement found in an open source

Certains monosyllabes gardent ainsi un accent fixe sur la syllabe radicale dans la forme définie, d'autres le reportent sur l'article (ou sur les préfixes possessifs ou démonstratifs).
new_statements.translation: In a polysyllabic word pronounced in isolation there is always one syllable set off by an expiratory accent, relatively weak and often hard to perceive. [...] The accent in any case has a very modest functional yield. [...] Nothing allows one to predict the place of the accent in a given word; all syllables can bear the accent. The situation is complicated by the fact that in morphological processes the accent of a form may move. Some monosyllables thus keep a fixed accent on the root syllable in the definite form, others throw it back onto the article (or onto the possessive or demonstrative prefixes).

new_statements.rule_in_words: Ubykh has a weak dynamic word stress, one per polysyllabic word in isolation, whose position is not predictable from phonological shape: any syllable may carry it, and it is lexically specified, with a small number of stress minimal pairs (asán 'it rots' vs ásan 'he sells it', etc.). Stress interacts with morphology: nouns split into a fixed-accent class (stress stays on the root when the definite article a- or possessive/demonstrative prefixes are added: bza 'language', def. abzá) and a mobile class (stress retracts onto the prefix: bža 'tongue', def. ábža; k'ʲabˤə́ 'wolf', def. ák'ʲab(ə)); fixed-accent items are about twice as numerous; the same opposition recurs in verb roots under causativisation. Dybo (1977: 43-44; 1989: 40-41) reanalyses exactly these facts as an Abkhaz-type dominant/recessive morpheme-valency system (stress at the end of the first string of dominant morphemes). Earlier first-hand authors concur that placement is free: Dirr 1928: 8 'Die Betonung scheint frei zu sein'; Mészáros 1934: 40-41 stress is meaning-distinguishing, article stressed in nominalised adjectives vs final stress in predicates.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Vogt: in connected speech words form accent groups under a single stress, some words losing their isolation stress (procliticisation), and 'un faible accent secondaire' appears within such groups (p. 32); he regards Mészáros's systematic marking of Nebenbetonung as unmotivated (p. 31). No word-internal secondary-stress rule is given.
new_statements.exceptions: Very low functional load; informants barely react to misplaced stress; notations of stress vary from text to text and author to author; a few disyllables stressed on the final move stress to their own first syllable rather than to the article (łapqə́ 'race', def. ałápq; nak'ʲə́ 'nail', def. anák'ʲ); unresolved divergent notations (aqáš 'the village' but aqašʁá 'in the village'); stressed syllables carry higher pitch except phrase-finally, where expiratory stress and pitch can disagree.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement concerns the word pronounced in isolation (citation forms from Tevfik Esenç); Vogt separately describes phrase-level accent groups in connected texts where isolated-word stresses can be lost. Stress is marked throughout the dictionary entries.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources describe the single Ubykh language (ubyk1235, ISO uby) as spoken by the émigré community in Turkey (Manyas district: Hacı Osman köyü etc.); Vogt's data are from the last fluent speaker Tevfik Esenç (1963), Mészáros calls the language 'Päkhy' (self-designation tʷaχə), Dirr's informant was from the Sapanca area. No dialect split relevant to stress is reported; glottocode ubyk1235 applies throughout.

tone.quote: Stress in Abkhaz-Abaza and Ubykh is markedly different, being mobile, distinctive and determined by inherent properties of morphemes … Abaza and Ubykh have stress systems basically identical to that of Abkhaz … The accentual class is a lexical property of each morpheme … Dybo et al. (1978) propose that such a system of stress assignment can have a tonal origin, claiming that Tapanta Abaza distinguishes high (dominant) and low (recessive) tone on stressed syllables; this, however, has not been confirmed by independent evidence.
tone.summary: Describes Ubykh prominence as mobile, morpheme-determined dynamic stress (dominant/recessive morphemes); the only tone remark is Dybo's unconfirmed tonal-origin hypothesis, stated for Tapanta Abaza.
tone.says: Describes Ubykh prominence as mobile, morpheme-determined dynamic stress (dominant/recessive morphemes); the only tone remark is Dybo's unconfirmed tonal-origin hypothesis, stated for Tapanta Abaza.

sources.citation: Чирикба, В. А. / Chirikba, Viacheslav A. 2024. Западнокавказский праязык: происхождение и этапы эволюционного развития / West Caucasian proto-language: Origin and stages of evolutionary development. Вопросы языкового родства / Journal of Language Relationship 22(3-4): 262-280.
sources.note: Hypothesizes that early Proto-West-Caucasian developed tones (compensating lost laryngeals/sonorants, distinguishing monosyllabic homophones; cites Dybo 1989) and that the evolution to late Common West Caucasian involved 'weakening of the role of tones and the emergence of a dynamic stress system' — i.e. the attested languages incl. Ubykh have dynamic stress, tone only reconstructed.
sources.venue: Вопросы языкового родства / Journal of Language Relationship

tone.quote: Эти последние, вероятно, могли различаться с помощью тонов (см. работу Дыбо 1989 о тональной гипотезе ЗК праязыка), появившихся на месте утраченных согласных (особенно ларингалов и сонантов). [...] Эволюция от раннего празападнокавказского языка в поздний общезападнокавказский состояла, по-видимому, в следующих процессах: — в фонологии: в ослаблении роли тонов и появлении системы динамического ударения; в появлении согласных кластеров из-за падения гласных в безударных слогах
tone.locator: second in the concluding list 'Эволюция от раннего празападнокавказского языка в поздний общезападнокавказский.. — в фонологии..' about 4; article header reads 'Journal of Language Relationship • Вопросы языкового родства • 22/3-4 (2024) • Pp. 262-280 • © В. А. Чирикба, 2024'
tone.translation: These [monosyllabic homophonous roots] could probably be distinguished by means of tones (see Dybo 1989 on the tonal hypothesis for the West Caucasian proto-language), which arose in place of lost consonants (especially laryngeals and sonorants). [...] The evolution from early Proto-West-Caucasian to late Common West Caucasian apparently consisted of the following processes: in phonology, the weakening of the role of tones and the emergence of a system of dynamic stress; the rise of consonant clusters through loss of vowels in unstressed syllables

tone.n_tones: None synchronically; unspecified reconstructed tones for early PWC

sources.citation: Дыбо, В. А. 2015. Парадигматические акцентные системы [Paradigmatic accent systems]. Вопросы языкознания 2015, № 3: 32-51.
sources.note: Classes the Ubykh (with Abkhaz, Abaza) accent system as a paradigmatic free-stress system that arose from a lost tone (register) system: stress was fixed on the last syllable of the first sequence of high-toned syllables (else word-final), then phonologized when the tones fell — i.e. synchronic Ubykh has stress, tone only in its reconstructed prehistory.

tone.quote: Разноместные ударения в балто-славянском и абхазо-убыхском следует объяснять фонологизацией акцентных контуров, явившейся следствием падения тонов, с которыми эти контуры были связаны [Дыбо 1973; 1977; 1978; 1989; Dybo et al. 1978; Николаев 1986а; 1989]. Специфика акцентных систем в этих языках объясняется первоначальными различиями в правилах фиксации акцента: в балто-славянском ударение ставилось на первом высокотоновом слоге или просто начальном слоге фонетического слова при отсутствии высокотоновых слогов, в абхазо-убыхском ударение стояло на последнем слоге первой последовательности высокотоновых слогов или просто на последнем слоге при отсутствии в фонетическом слове высокотоновых слогов.
tone.locator: pp. 34-35, section on morphonologized accent systems; list naming 'убыхская' on p. 35-36
tone.translation: The free (variable-place) stresses of Balto-Slavic and Abkhaz-Ubykh are to be explained by the phonologization of accent contours resulting from the loss of the tones with which those contours were associated [...]. The specifics of the accent systems in these languages follow from original differences in the accent-fixing rule: in Balto-Slavic stress fell on the first high-toned syllable (or simply the initial syllable when the phonetic word had no high-toned syllable); in Abkhaz-Ubykh stress stood on the last syllable of the first sequence of high-toned syllables, or simply on the last syllable when the phonetic word had no high-toned syllables.
tone.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone.n_tones: Synchronically none; reconstructed pre-West-Caucasian high vs low (register) sy…
tone.says: Classes the Ubykh (with Abkhaz, Abaza) accent system as a paradigmatic free-stress system that arose from a lost tone (register) system: stress was fixed on the last syllable of the first sequence of high-toned syllables (else word-final), then phonologized when the tones fell — i.e. synchronic Ubykh has stress, tone only in its reconstructed prehistory.

Značenie zapadnokavkazskoj akcentnoj sistemy dlja izučenija balto-slavjanskoj i japonskix akcentnyx sistem [The value of the West Caucasian accentual system for the study of the Balto-Slavic and Japanese accentual systems]. DOI 10.1163/9789401200325_005.
sources.note: Describes Ubykh word prosody as a mobile stress system with two accent paradigms (dominant/recessive morphemes); tone appears only as the hypothesised lost source of that system; no tone inventory.
sources.venue: Studies in Slavic and General Linguistics 37

tone.quote: Сходство тоновых схем этих языков и порождавшихся ими акцентных парадигм с балтославянскими акцентными парадигмами и побудило меня выдвинуть тональную гипотезу происхождения парадигматических акцентных систем … Такой системой является западнокавказская (абхазская и убыхская). К чему это приводит? 1) Системы парадигматического акцента возникают в результате деформации демаркационного (разграничительного) акцента действием доминатных слогов и дальнейшей фонологизации этой деформации в результате падения фонологического различия между доминантными и рецессивными слогами.
tone.locator: pp. 79-80; Ubykh accent passage with Table 2, p. 76
tone.translation: The similarity of the tone patterns of these languages [Kanuri, Tubu] and of the accent paradigms they generated to the Balto-Slavic accent paradigms is what prompted me to put forward the tonal hypothesis of the origin of paradigmatic accent systems … Such a system is the West Caucasian one (Abkhaz and Ubykh). What does this lead to? 1) Systems of paradigmatic accent arise from the deformation of a demarcative (delimiting) accent by the action of dominant syllables and the subsequent phonologization of this deformation as a result of the loss of the phonological distinction between dominant and recessive syllables.
tone.summary: Describes Ubykh word prosody as a mobile stress system with two accent paradigms (dominant/recessive morphemes); tone appears only as the hypothesised lost source of that system; no tone inventory.
tone.says: Describes Ubykh word prosody as a mobile stress system with two accent paradigms (dominant/recessive morphemes); tone appears only as the hypothesised lost source of that system; no tone inventory.

In: Lingvističeskaja komparativistika v kul'turnom i istoričeskom aspektax, 88-113. Moskva: Moskovskij gosudarstvennyj universitet. Open PDF (author's institute page, Institut slavjanovedenija RAN):https://inslav.ru/images/stories/people/dybo/dybo2007.pdf
sources.note: Treats Ubykh as a paradigmatic (dominant/recessive) mobile stress-accent system like Abkhaz; whether these systems keep a tonal basis is raised only for the group (Starostin's checks) and left open.
sources.venue: Lingvističeskaja komparativistika v kul'turnom i istoričeskom aspektax

tone.quote: Три дочерних системы — абхазская, тапантская и убыхская — сохранили все её основные (системообразущие) параметры … могут демонстрироваться как образцы «чистой» парадигматической акцентной системы. Эта их особенность вызывала недоверие к чисто акцентному их характеру, чтó привело к ряду проверок с целью обнаружить сохранение тонового их основания. Проверка бзыбского состояния, проведенная С. А. Старостиным, привела к отрицательным результатам, в тапантском диалекте ему как будто удалось обнаружить слабые тоны.
tone.translation: The three daughter systems - Abkhaz, Tapanta and Ubykh - have preserved all its basic (system-forming) parameters ... they can be exhibited as specimens of a 'pure' paradigmatic accent system. This feature of theirs aroused distrust of their purely accentual character, which led to a series of checks aimed at detecting a preserved tonal basis. The check of the Bzyb state carried out by S. A. Starostin gave negative results; in the Tapanta dialect he apparently managed to detect weak tones.
tone.summary: Treats Ubykh as a paradigmatic (dominant/recessive) mobile stress-accent system like Abkhaz; whether these systems keep a tonal basis is raised only for the group (Starostin's checks) and left open.

sources.note: Second-hand via Vogt 1963 (held): the article reduces Ubykh vocalism to two fundamental vowels /a/ and /ə/ with rules for their timbres, and (p. 201) suggests a possible influence of the accent -- under the accent the timbre would be rather [a] than [ä] (ex. 'herbe', 'petit') -- which Vogt thinks runs the other way; a single stress-conditioned-allophony remark, nothing on tone; content itself unseen.

sources.note: Record plus Vogt 1963 second-hand (held txt): Dumézil's phonological statement of the Ubykh sound system (Vogt cites it as 'SS', pp. 163, 167, for retroflexion and vowel resonance); Vogt p. 31 notes that Dumézil marks the place of the accent in the texts appended to this article (pp. 173-189) but drops accent marking when re-editing the same texts -- so it is one of the few accent-marked Ubykh sources; a stress language, no tone description expected; content itself unseen.
